The module ignores the house style the rest of the app adopted

Every notices and litigation screen uses its own NoticesPageHeader / NoticesCardHeader, 10 px uppercase headers and raw palette colours, while Filing Status, GSTR-1/3B, Builder, Annual Return and the reports moved to the 9/9C workspace theme this month.
PageHeader compact, WS_* table classes, KpiTile, SectionCard, the readable Badge and semantic tokens only (docs/UI-UX-REDESIGN.md).
Floating chrome covers the actions

The fixed notification bell (MainLayout.tsx:69) sits on the right-most header button on every page (Sync All, Add Notice, Create Matter, Export, PDF); the Quick-actions and Chat buttons cover table columns and form buttons.
Put the bell in the header row (or reserve md:pr-12), add bottom padding to <main>, merge the two floating buttons into one speed-dial on phones.
Phone layout breaks
The module tab bar widens every page to about 485 px at 390 px; the drawer’s close button goes off-screen; 8-column tables are cut; ₹ figures overflow their tiles.
Scrollable / wrapping tab bar, card lists below md, compact ₹ L / cr figures with the full value on hover.
Navigation is mislabelled and forgets context
“Matters” opens a filtered notice list and “Hearings” opens Litigation Matters; there is no hearings page; tabs and filters live in component state, so Back, e-mails and shared links lose them.
One nav (Command centre · Work queue · Notices · Matters · Hearings · Calendar · Clients · Reports) and URL-persisted tabs and filter chips with a clear-all.
One notice, three disconnected places
Stage and owner live in the drawer, portal items and hearings in the case folder, money and hearings in the matter — none links to the others, and the drawer fails in production.
The Notice workspace at /notices/:id pulling the folder, matter, documents, deadlines and payments into one page (target mock-up, §7).
Screens are read-only at the moment of decision
No Log reply, Assign, Request extension, Retry sync, Update password or Reopen where the user is looking at the problem; e-mails have no link back to the notice.
Give every status one primary next action, on the row and on the page; every e-mail gets an “Open notice” button.
Numbers disagree between sibling screens

On one fictional test data set: Overdue 14 (tile) vs 69 (its list); companies 11 vs 12; failed logins 2 vs 5; notices 182 vs 186; exposure ₹ 4.23 cr vs ₹ 3.68 cr; “closed” defined four ways and outstanding money computed four ways in litigation.
One notice_facts and one matter_facts view feeding every screen, with an “as of” time and a definition tooltip on every number.
Raw codes and four vocabularies

Portal types and codes become titles (“Notice”, “Voluntary_payment”, “auto:refund_order”, “Closed: paid”); four stage vocabularies; open stages shown green; filed refunds green while an RFD-08 show-cause is grey.
A display-title map per form code, one stage enum, one status-tone map (overdue / action = red, waiting = amber, filed = blue, closed = green / grey).
Six date formats and mixed money formats
05/10/2026, 09-09-2026, 2026-10-07, ‘5/10/2026, 7:43:00 am’, ‘20 Sept 2026’ and ‘18h ago’ side by side; hearing times captured but never shown.
One fmtDate (dd Mon yyyy, IST) with time where it matters, one fmtMoney, relative time only in activity feeds.
Machine text and silent failures
Postgres errors in toasts (“null value in column portal_key …”), extension messages (“Receiving end does not exist”), raw key dumps; failed loads shown as empty tabs, “Matter not found” or ₹ 0.
A message catalogue (code → plain sentence + next step) and real error states with Retry; never render a failed query as zero.
Irreversible actions without confirmation, undo or permission
Bulk Close, inline Open/Closed, the sweep and Close Matter act at once; litigation screens ignore the permission keys the notice screens use.
useConfirm() with a reason, an Undo toast, preview counts for sweeps, and the existing can*() gates on every edit and export.
Keyboard and screen-reader access
KPI tiles, category rows, calendar days and count cells are clickable divs / <td> without focus; icon-only buttons have no labels.
Real buttons and links, aria-label on every icon button, visible focus rings, open-in-new-tab on counts.
Portal-parity clutter hides the key facts
The case folder shows 4–6 “There are no records to display” sections and raw key dumps, while the due date, hearing and DRC-07A recovery demand sit last.
Hide empty sections; typed fact cards first (due date, hearing, demand by head, reply status), raw portal JSON behind a disclosure.
E-mails are not actionable
Staff alerts greet the client and sign off as the recipient, show ISO dates and bare references, and carry no link; the limitation alert shows a stale due date beside the real deadline.
Separate internal and client templates, a deep-link button, formatted dates, client and notice named in the subject.
Automation is exposed as manual buttons
Sync All, Send digest and “run the closing sweep” are buttons a person must remember; the sweep errors in production.
Run them on schedule and after each sync; keep “Run now” on the Portal Autopilot page only.
Litigation writes bypass the shared library
Pages write matters directly, so no events are logged, matter numbers come from two generators, pre-deposits are dropped and lists sort by creation date.
Route every write through src/lib/litigationData.ts; one numbering function; sort by next deadline.
